claims.text: The superconducting properties of the proposed uncharacterized high-entropy alloys are primarily controlled by average electron–phonon coupling strength.
Local lattice distortion strongly modulates average electron–phonon coupling strength.
Larger atomic-size mismatches and random site occupancy create greater local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions lower phonon frequencies.
Lower phonon frequencies caused by local distortions enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling raises the superconducting transition temperature.
The starting material is a homogeneous, as-cast, single-phase high-entropy alloy made by rapid solidification.
The alloy contains at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
Controlled annealing can modestly reduce local lattice distortions by enhancing short-range ordering without causing phase separation or significant segregation.
Reducing local lattice distortion through annealing decreases electron–phonon coupling.
The annealing-induced decrease in electron–phonon coupling leads to a reduction in superconducting transition temperature.
The proposed distortion-mediated mechanism dominates over effects attributable solely to overall electron count.
Annealed samples with reduced local lattice distortion will have a measurably lower superconducting transition temperature than the as-cast material.
Annealing will produce narrower XRD peaks and reduced EXAFS local-strain signatures.
The structural indicators of reduced distortion will correlate with the lower transition temperature.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to single-phase, chemically disordered alloys with at least five constituents at 5 atomic percent or more that remain free of significant phase separation.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when annealing causes long-range ordering or secondary-phase precipitation.
Disorder-enhanced electron scattering may complicate the relationship between lattice order and superconducting properties.
The experiment compares identically composed as-cast and annealed samples using XRD, EXAFS, four-point resistivity, and SQUID magnetometry.
The hypothesis is falsified if verified reduction of local distortion after annealing is not accompanied by a lower transition temperature, including if the transition temperature increases.
